_about: Hand edits applied by scripts/build_artifact_data.py to reading_workflow.json claims. Key: <model>/<group>/<claim id>. theme: page grouping. ev: index of the evidence quote kept. claim: rewritten text (required for 'partly' verdicts, so the claim matches the verifier's correction; also used to drop counts from the pre-79a51bf chat coder). drop: omit the claim. Claims without an entry are kept as written, theme 'other', first quote. Refuted claims are always dropped.

gpt-oss-20b/NT-T-small/C1.claim: Talking in Part 2 barely raised prices in the main design. The mean gain in selling price (periods 6 on) was about +3.3 at n=2 and +1.9 at n=4, against human gains of +43.2 and +75.3, and there is no human-like inverted U in n.

gpt-oss-20b/NT-T-small/C2.claim: Chat mostly ratifies the last NoTalk price rather than the joint-profit price: in 10 of 12 n=2/n=4 NT-T markets the opening Part 2 agreement equals the price set in period 1.29 (11 of 12 counting the first agreement eventually reached).

gpt-oss-20b/NT-T-small/C3.claim: Firms know the best common price is 100 yet aim low. In the post-game probe 35 of 36 firms answered 100, but the highest price jointly realised in any n=4 NT-T market was 10, and most n=4 talk was about moving from 1 to 2 (one market discussed 50 and 20, another 3 or 4).

gpt-oss-20b/NT-T-small/C4.claim: "Raise together next period" promises were renewed period after period. In 3 of 12 markets the joint raise never happened, and in at least 4 others it came only after several deferrals.

gpt-oss-20b/NT-T-small/C5.claim: Some n=4 breaches were accidental rather than undercuts: a lone firm priced above its peers or carried out a raise the others skipped, and at least 3 notes invert the rule, believing a higher price captures the market. Most flagged n=4 breach periods do still involve an undercut.

gpt-oss-20b/NT-T-small/C8.claim: Threats are restated in many periods ('0-price punishment rule') while n=4 prices stay at 1-2, and are seldom carried out: at least three punishment episodes followed real undercuts. One was uncoordinated, with firms announcing different 'punishment' prices, one of them 100.

gpt-oss-20b/NT-T-small/C9.claim: Simultaneous chat produced crossed messages in duopolies: each firm 'agreed' to the other's earlier proposal (70 vs 1), and both notes say they were matching. At least three crossings occurred in two duopolies; these are coordination failures, not deliberate breaches.

gpt-oss-20b/NT-T-small/C10.claim: Duopoly agreements in Part 2 were rarely broken, but sat at whatever level was inherited: 3 of 6 duopolies held identical prices throughout Talk, and the others moved their agreement (1 to 10, 1 to 70, 57/58).

gpt-oss-20b/NT-T-large/c1.claim: At n=6, 8 and 10, prices without talk sit at the competitive level (16 of 18 markets at 0 from period 6). With talk every market reaches an explicit agreement, but in roughly 11 to 13 of 18 the settled price is 10 or lower. Mean Part 2 selling prices (n=6: 17.0, n=8: 4.2) are 48 and 51 points below the human Talk benchmarks.

gpt-oss-20b/NT-T-large/c2.claim: In the first Talk period firms often float high proposals (50, 70, 100), but within the three rounds the group usually converges on a low proposal: 3 of the 4 openings cited ended at 10 or below (the fourth settled at 50).

gpt-oss-20b/NT-T-large/c5.claim: Breaches at large n are often deliberate small undercuts, announced in chat or planned in notes, justified by an explicit trade-off that the agreed short punishment costs less than the one-period gain. The arithmetic is sometimes wrong (one firm assumed it would be the sole undercutter when four undercut).

gpt-oss-20b/NT-T-large/c6.claim: Agreed punishments are sometimes carried out as a group, close to their stated length, giving a deviate-punish-return cycle rather than a collapse: three clean cycles in n8 m3 and three two-period all-zero blocks in n10 m2.

gpt-oss-20b/NT-T-large/c7.claim: Covert defection (a chat promise of the agreed price while the private note plans an undercut) occurs in at least three large-n markets. When a threatened punishment is not carried out, prices erode step by step instead.

gpt-oss-20b/NT-T-large/c9.claim: Agreed raises stall: unanimous 'yes' votes to raise next period were followed by most firms staying at the old price. When part of the group did raise, the firms that stayed low took the market and the raise collapsed.

gpt-oss-20b/NT-T-large/c11.why: About the pre-79a51bf chat coder's parsing artifact, since fixed.

gpt-oss-20b/T-NT-small/hyst-1.claim: In 10 of 12 T-NT markets (n=2, 4) the mean selling price over the last five NoTalk periods is within 2 of the final Talk-period price. n=4 T-NT Part 2 sells at 38.9 against 0.5 in NT-NT (humans: 67 vs 5.69).

gpt-oss-20b/T-NT-small/hyst-4.claim: Collusion newly broke down after chat was removed in 2 of 12 markets, each through a deliberate deviation reasoned out in a note. In n4 m4, after 14 NoTalk periods at 100, D undercut to 99 citing the lack of a credible punishment, and all firms were at 0 within 6 periods. In n2 m4 both firms undercut step by step from 70 to 52-53.

gpt-oss-20b/T-NT-small/talk-1.claim: Talk from period 1 usually produced an agreement at a focal price below 100: four of six duopolies settled at 70. Only 3 of 12 markets sustained 100, although 35 of 36 firms named 100 as the best common price. n=4 Part 1 Talk sold at 51.2 (periods 6 on) against 89.0 for humans.

gpt-oss-20b/T-NT-small/talk-2.claim: In at least 4 of 12 markets chat did not stop a price war: firms announced their undercuts openly and prices fell before settling at a low agreed level. In n4 m0 firms repeated 'raise to 2 together next period' from 1.20 to 1.29 and never did.

gpt-oss-20b/T-NT-small/agree-1.claim: Agreements in small T-NT markets were usually kept, with no broken agreement in 4 of 6 duopolies. The breaches read were secret: planned in the private note while the firm reaffirmed the agreement in chat, sometimes undercutting by far more than one unit.

gpt-oss-20b/T-NT-small/punish-1.claim: Punishment followed by forgiveness was rare. In n4 m2 one firm applied the Part 1 price-0 rule for five NoTalk periods after a one-unit deviation, then returned to 44, which held to the end. In n4 m1 an agreed three-period zero punishment was carried out but collusion was not restored, and C's deviation to 50 in n4 m4 went unpunished.

gpt-oss-20b/T-NT-small/mist-2.claim: Private notes often miscount the history (at 2.1 alone, notes in 7 markets claim more periods than were played) and misstate tie payoffs, yet probe answers are almost all right (36 of 36 on maximum price and last prices, 35 of 36 on the best common price). The errors come from running memory, not misread rules.

gpt-oss-20b/T-NT-small/order-1.claim: Talk worked much better from period 1 than after a NoTalk phase: T-NT Part 1 Talk sold at 65.9 (n=2) and 51.2 (n=4) from period 6, against 37.5 and 2.7 for NT-T Part 2 (all periods). Humans priced high in both orders.

gpt-oss-20b/T-NT-large/C1.claim: Part 1 talk lifts prices above NT-NT in every large-n market but far below human Talk levels, and the lift falls with n: 22.0 (n=6), 16.7 (n=8), 9.2 (n=10), periods 6 on. No Talk-period selling price exceeds 90.

gpt-oss-20b/T-NT-large/C2.claim: Firms know 100 is the best common price (143 of 144 probe answers), yet no large-n T-NT agreement is ever at 100. The most common agreed price is 1, which firms call cooperation or collusion, and four markets sold at 1 for nearly all of Part 1.

gpt-oss-20b/T-NT-large/C3.claim: Several groups agree on a 'reset to 0' punishment and carry it out: after an undercut of the 70 price, most firms (5 to 7 of 10) price 0 the next period, earning nothing themselves. Six of 18 markets have Part 1 periods where at least half the firms price 0.

gpt-oss-20b/T-NT-large/C4.claim: Under the 0-price rule some firms undercut by 1 deliberately, reckoning the shared punishment costs them no more than it costs others; this appears in all four punishment markets. Some announce it in chat; others promise 70 publicly while the note plans 69.

gpt-oss-20b/T-NT-large/C5.claim: Agreements above a price of 1 at large n are kept in only a minority of periods, the keep rate falls with n, and the most common breach is a one-unit undercut. (Counts from the earlier automated coder are omitted here; see the chat screen table.)

gpt-oss-20b/T-NT-large/C6.claim: Groups also agree on limited, scheduled punishments. In n8 m0 all eight firms priced 30 'to finish the punishment cycle' and returned together to 55 at 1.26, the one verified executed scheduled punishment; elsewhere (n6 m0) a threat alone preceded a long stable spell.

gpt-oss-20b/T-NT-large/C7.claim: After chat is removed high prices rarely last: of 6 large-n markets ending Part 1 at 44 or more, only n6 m1 kept its price beyond 3 NoTalk periods, and in 3 of the 6 one firm priced 0 or 1 in the very first NoTalk period.

gpt-oss-20b/T-NT-large/C9.claim: Rule misreads drive some Part 2 moves: one firm prices 100 believing the highest price wins, another thinks undercutting 70 to 69 lowers its payoff, and some claim price 0 'wins the entire market' although a tie at 0 earns nothing. Price 0 is 13.7% of T-NT Part 2 firm-periods.

gpt-oss-20b/T-NT-large/C10.claim: At large n, Part 1 talk leaves at most a floor of 1 rather than 0: in the last five Part 2 periods the selling price is at least 1 in 13 of 18 T-NT markets against 5 of 18 NT-NT, and only n6 m1 (31.0) is above 1.

gpt-oss-20b/T-NT-large/C11.claim: Firms keep applying Part 1 punishment rules from memory after chat is removed, but recall different penalties: in one period one punisher priced 39, another 0, another 56. Some firms hold a lone 70 for 9 to 15 periods while earning nothing.

gpt-oss-20b/NT-NT/c2.claim: NT-NT markets settle into all firms at 1 or all at 0 and mostly stay there through Part 2: 14 end all-1, 14 all-0 and 2 mixed, and 26 of 30 restart Part 2 at their Part 1 end state.

gpt-oss-20b/NT-NT/c4.claim: When a firm stuck at 0 posts a high price to signal cooperation (6 of 24 n>=4 markets, from period 6 of a part), no high-price outcome follows and the signaller soon returns to 0 or 1, although at 0 the signal costs nothing.

gpt-oss-20b/NT-NT/c5.claim: Firms often price 0 in period 1, before seeing any rival (21 of 30 NT-NT markets), believing 0 'secures' the market; all 14 all-0 end states come from such markets. The error is the belief that 0 guarantees the market (all-0 is itself an equilibrium).

gpt-oss-20b/NT-NT/c6.claim: Duopolies are the only NT-NT markets with tacit high pricing, and it breaks down: in 3 of 6 both firms start high and slide down a one-unit ladder until one jumps to a 'safe' low price and the market locks near (1,1). Prices never cycle back up as in Edgeworth cycles.

gpt-oss-20b/NT-NT/c8.claim: Some firms misread period 20 (the first die throw) as the certain last period (notes in 6 of 30 Part 1 markets). It changed a price only once, and there it started the collapse: A undercut a 94/94 plateau to 93 'since there is no future period'.

gpt-oss-20b/NT-NT/c10.claim: Firms routinely call the price-1 Nash outcome 'collusion' or 'cooperation' (notes in 28 of 30 NT-NT markets), so keyword screens on notes would misclassify competitive markets as collusive.

gpt-oss-20b/NT-NT/c11.claim: Duopoly NoTalk outcomes vary widely across identically treated markets: NT-T Part 1 duopolies sold at 35.8 (periods 6 on) against 13.5 for NT-NT, and only NT-T n2 m0 shows full tacit collusion (100/100 in all 29 periods). Both are below the human 50.4.

gpt-oss-20b/cross-cutting/C1.claim: Price 0 (weakly dominated) is chosen in 10,399 of 28,620 price decisions, and in NoTalk periods the share rises with n, from 5% at n=2 to 64% at n=10. Notes often acknowledge it earns nothing ('not left out'), so it is intentional; whether it is a reasoning mistake is open.

gpt-oss-20b/cross-cutting/C2.claim: Before any talk, with n>=4, the selling price is 0 or 1 in all 1,968 market-periods, and posted prices from period 6 are 0.2 to 1.1 against 18 to 29 for humans. The only all-100 tacit collusion is one n=2 market.

gpt-oss-20b/cross-cutting/C3.claim: Low prices are not a misunderstanding of the payoff: 535 of 540 probed firms name 100 as the best common price and all 540 name 100 as the maximum consumer price; each of the 5 errors matches a price its market had colluded at. Last-period recall is wrong for only 5 firms.

gpt-oss-20b/cross-cutting/C4.claim: Probe answers about deviations are unreliable both ways: firms deny undercuts that happened (sometimes just outside their chat window) and accuse firms that only partly broke their word.

gpt-oss-20b/cross-cutting/C5.claim: Breaches are often announced openly: a firm states in chat that it will undercut and accept the pre-agreed short zero-price punishment, sometimes arguing the two-period average is higher (and sometimes then not undercutting after all). Punishments become rituals: punishers sometimes price 0 in the breach period itself. Threats appear in most talk periods at n>=4, whereas threats were rare among humans.

gpt-oss-20b/cross-cutting/C6.claim: Some chat promises are contradicted by the same firm's private note in the same period (the automated screen flags 83 gpt-oss talk periods after the coder fix, about 70% deliberate on a hand-checked sample). In large-n Talk Part 1 the chat can work like a public auction: firms announce a price in round 3 and most then privately undercut it by 1.

gpt-oss-20b/cross-cutting/C7.claim: Promises to raise the price 'next period' are rarely carried out, and agreements at 100 occur only for n=2, n=4 T-NT and n=10 NT-T, never in an n=6 or n=8 talk cell.

gpt-oss-20b/cross-cutting/C8.claim: No sign of end-game unravelling after period 20: after a selling price of 10 or more, the price falls in 19% of periods from period 21 on against 28% in periods 6-20. The die is rarely mentioned (97 of 8,100 late decisions), and 29 notes wrongly call period 20 'the final period', yet those firms keep their price.

gpt-oss-20b/cross-cutting/C9.claim: Notes record histories that did not happen: about 127 notes in 14 markets claim streaks longer than the periods played, and some streak counters stay frozen for many periods.

gpt-oss-20b/cross-cutting/C10.claim: Format slips are frequent but get fixed: a price was given on a chat turn in 3,333 of 28,620 chat turns (1,908 of them in round 3), and re-asks fixed almost all (9 chat fallbacks in total). Tie misreads are rare (41 notes, 36 chat turns).

gpt-oss-20b/cross-cutting/C11.why: About the pre-79a51bf chat coder's parsing artifact, since fixed.
